copy.tl: Hindi lang dahon ang berde — pati damo at lumot sa tubig ay berde sa parehong dahilan: lahat sila'y gumagamit ng chlorophyll para gumawa ng pagkain mula sa liwanag!
copy.bis: Dili lang dahon ang berde — apil ang sagbot ug lumot sa tubig berde sa samang rason: silang tanan naggamit og chlorophyll aron maghimo og pagkaon gikan sa kahayag!

Can a red leaf still make its own food?

Yes! Red leaves still hide green chlorophyll underneath a red pigment, so they keep making food — it's just covered up.

Kung pula ang dahon, gumagana pa ba ang photosynthesis?

Oo! May chlorophyll pa rin sa loob ng pulang dahon, natatakpan lang ng pulang pigment. Patuloy pa rin itong gumagawa ng pagkain.

Kon pula ang dahon, naghimo pa ba kini og kaugalingong pagkaon?

Oo! Aduna gihapon chlorophyll sa sulod sa pula nga dahon, natabonan lang sa pula nga pigment. Padayon gihapon kining naghimo og pagkaon.

What's special about leech saliva?

A leech's saliva is like a tiny medicine kit—one part numbs pain, one stops clotting, and one widens blood vessels, all helping it feed!

Ano ang espesyal sa laway ng linta?

Ang laway ng linta ay parang maliit na kahon ng gamot—may pampamanhid ng sakit, may pumipigil sa pamumuo ng dugo, at may nagpapalapad ng ugat, lahat tumutulong habang ito ay kumakain!

Unsay espesyal sa laway sa alimatok?

Ang laway sa alimatok sama sa gamayng kahon sa tambal—naa'y magpamanhid sa sakit, naa'y magpugong sa pagbara sa dugo, ug naa'y magpalapad sa ugat, tanan makatabang samtang mokaon kini!

Is a leech related to the earthworm?

copy.bis:
Paryente ba sa earthworm ang leech?

Oo -- parehas silang segmented worm sa phylum nga Annelida! Pero lahi sila og klase, mao nga dili sila magkapamilya.

Where can lichen still survive?

Lichen can live in tough places like high mountains and freezing lands, where almost nothing else can grow.

Saan pa kaya mabuhay ang lichen?

Kayang mabuhay ng lichen sa mahihirap na lugar tulad ng matataas na bundok at malamig na lupain, kung saan halos wala nang ibang tumutubo.

Asa pa makalahutay ang lichen?

Makalahutay ang lichen sa lisod nga mga dapit sama sa taas nga bukid ug bugnaw nga yuta, diin hapit wala nay laing motubo.

assignedReviews.reason: The card states the speed of sound but does not explore or describe how sound is made or transferred in everyday situations. It provides a numerical fact about sound speed, not the mechanism or everyday examples of sound production/transfer.

copy.en: Mach 1 is the speed of sound — about 1,225 kilometers per hour at sea level. Super sonic!
copy.tl: Ang Mach 1 ay bilis ng tunog — mga 1,225 kilometro kada oras sa lebel ng dagat. Super bilis!
copy.bis: Ang Mach 1 mao ang kakusog sa tingog — mga 1,225 ka kilometro kada oras sa lebel sa dagat. Super kusog!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Our body needs three main nutrients in large amounts: protein, carbohydrates, and fats.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify the basic needs of all living things, such as air, food, water, and shelter
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes specific macronutrients (protein, carbohydrates, fats) that the body needs, but does not identify food, air, water, or shelter as basic needs of living things. It is related to the topic of food but does not directly support the competency's skill of identifying basic needs.

copy.en: Our body needs three main nutrients in large amounts: protein, carbohydrates, and fats.
copy.tl: Tatlo ang pangunahing sustansyang kailangan ng katawan sa malaking dami: protina, karbohaydrat, at taba.
copy.bis: Tulo ang nag-unang sustansya nga gikinahanglan sa lawas sa dako nga gidaghanon: protina, karbohaydrat, ug tambok.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Magnets come in fun different shapes, like a straight bar, a horseshoe, and a round ring!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: carry out guided investigations to identify the properties of magnets, including how they affect other magnets and objects made of different materials
assignedReviews.reason: The card only describes magnet shapes. It does not address properties of magnets, their effects on other magnets, or effects on objects made of different materials, which are the core actions of G4-F-7.

copy.en: Magnets come in fun different shapes, like a straight bar, a horseshoe, and a round ring!
copy.tl: May iba't ibang hugis ang magnet, gaya ng bar, parang horseshoe, at bilog na ring!
copy.bis: Ang mga magnet adunay lainlaing porma, sama sa bar, horseshoe, ug lingin nga ring!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The motors inside them use electromagnets!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: make a simple electromagnet and observe and record its properties
assignedReviews.reason: The card only mentions that motors use electromagnets and that changing push/pull keeps the motor spinning. It does not instruct making a simple electromagnet or observing/recording its properties, which is the core action of the competency.

copy.en:
What makes fans and battery toys spin so fast?

The motors inside them use electromagnets! The changing push and pull of the magnet keeps the motor spinning fast.
copy.tl:
Ano ang nagpapaikot nang mabilis sa mga bentilador at de-bateryang laruan?

Ang mga motor sa loob nila ay gumagamit ng electromagnet! Ang pabago-bagong tulak at hila ng magnet ang nagpapaikot nang mabilis.
copy.bis:
Unsa ang nagpatuyok pagdali sa mga bentilador ug dula nga de-baterya?

Ang mga motor sa sulod niini naggamit ug electromagnet! Ang nagbalhinbalhin nga duso ug bira sa magnet maoy nagpatuyok pagdali.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: All around a magnet is an invisible region of force called a magnetic field!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: carry out guided investigations to identify the properties of magnets, including how they affect other magnets and objects made of different materials
assignedReviews.reason: The card only states that a magnetic field is an invisible region of force around a magnet. It does not support the guided investigation of magnet properties or how magnets affect other magnets and objects made of different materials.

copy.en: All around a magnet is an invisible region of force called a magnetic field!
copy.tl: Sa palibot ng magneto ay may di-nakikitang larangan ng puwersa na tinatawag na magnetic field!
copy.bis: Sa palibot sa magneto adunay dili makita nga dapit sa puwersa nga gitawag og magnetic field!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: It is a natural magnet found in the wild called lodestone.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: carry out guided investigations to identify the properties of magnets, including how they affect other magnets and objects made of different materials
assignedReviews.reason: The card only states that lodestone is a natural magnet. It does not describe any properties of magnets, nor how magnets affect other magnets or objects made of different materials, and it does not support carrying out guided investigations. This is background vocabulary about magnets, not direct instruction for the competency.

copy.en: Nature has its own special magnet! It is a natural magnet found in the wild called lodestone.
copy.tl: May likas na magneto sa ating kalikasan! Ito ay isang espesyal na bato na tinatawag na lodestone.
copy.bis: Adunay kaugalingong magneto ang atong kinaiyahan! Kini usa ka kinaiyanhon nga bato nga gitawag og lodestone.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A permanent magnet stays strong forever. A temporary one, like a clip, only becomes magnetic while touching a real magnet
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: carry out guided investigations to identify the properties of magnets, including how they affect other magnets and objects made of different materials
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes a property of magnets (permanent vs temporary), but the competency specifically requires guided investigations to identify properties including how magnets affect other magnets and objects made of different materials. The card does not address interactions with other magnets or different materials, and it does not support the investigation aspect. It is only tangentially related to magnet properties.

copy.en: There are two kinds of magnets! A permanent magnet stays strong forever. A temporary one, like a clip, only becomes magnetic while touching a real magnet — once removed, it quickly loses its strength.
copy.tl: May dalawang uri ng magnet! Ang permanent magnet ay laging malakas. Ang temporary, tulad ng clip, nagiging magnetiko lang habang nakadikit sa totoong magnet — pag-alis, mabilis nawawala ang lakas.
copy.bis: Adunay duha ka klase sa magnet! Ang permanent magnet kanunay kusgan. Ang temporary, sama sa clip, nahimong magnetiko lang samtang nagdikit sa tinuod nga magnet — kung tangtangon, dali nawala ang kusog.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: As Earth spins, hot liquid iron in the core swirls and creates electric currents.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: create a scale drawing to represent relative thicknesses of the layers of Earth's interior, including the crust, lithosphere, asthenosphere, mantle, outer core, and inner core
assignedReviews.reason: The card explains the dynamo mechanism that generates Earth's magnetic field. It does not address the relative thicknesses of Earth's interior layers (crust, lithosphere, asthenosphere, mantle, outer core, inner core) nor a scale drawing, which are the explicit requirements of G9-E-8. The only connection is the mention of the core, making it related to Earth's interior but not directly supporting the competency.

copy.en: As Earth spins, hot liquid iron in the core swirls and creates electric currents. This moving iron makes our magnetic field! Scientists call it the dynamo.
copy.tl: Habang umiikot ang Daigdig, ang mainit na likidong bakal sa core ay umiikot at lumilikha ng kuryente. Ito ang gumagawa ng magnetic field! Tinatawag itong dynamo.
copy.bis: Samtang nagtuyok ang Kalibutan, ang init ug likido nga puthaw sa core nagtuyok ug naghimo ug kuryente. Kini ang nagbuhat sa magnetic field! Gitawag ni nga dynamo.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: named after the brilliant Nikola Tesla!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use information from secondary sources to identify a famous Filipino and/or foreign scientist and their invention/s
assignedReviews.reason: The card identifies Nikola Tesla as a foreign scientist but does not mention any invention of his. The competency requires identifying a scientist and their invention(s). The tesla unit is not an invention, so the card only shares the scientist's name without the required invention detail.

copy.en:
What unit measures the strength of a magnetic field?

It's measured in teslas (T), named after the brilliant Nikola Tesla!
copy.tl:
Anong yunit ang sumusukat ng lakas ng magnetic field?

Sinusukat ito sa teslas (T), na ipinangalan kay Nikola Tesla!
copy.bis:
Unsa nga yunit ang nagsukod sa kusog sa magnetic field?

Gisukod kini sa teslas (T), nga ginganlan kang Nikola Tesla!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Magnetoreception — the sense of Earth's magnetic field! Humans don't have it, but birds, turtles, and fish use it to feel direction.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use information from secondary sources to describe examples of how some animals have changed to better suit their environment, such as mimicry or camouflage
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes a sensory ability (magnetoreception) that some animals possess, but it does not describe how animals have changed over time to better suit their environment, which is the core of G5-L-9 (adaptation such as mimicry or camouflage). The content is only tangentially related to animal traits and does not directly support the competency.

copy.en:
What sense do humans not have but birds do?

Magnetoreception — the sense of Earth's magnetic field! Humans don't have it, but birds, turtles, and fish use it to feel direction.
copy.tl:
Anong pandama ang wala sa tao pero meron sa ibon?

Magnetoreception — ang pakiramdam sa magnetic field! Wala ito sa tao, pero meron ang ibon, pawikan, at isda para makaramdam ng direksyon.
copy.bis:
Unsa nga pandama ang wala sa tawo apan naa sa langgam?

Magnetoreception — ang pagbati sa magnetic field! Wala kini sa tawo, apan naa sa pipila ka mananap sama sa langgam, pawikan, ug isda aron makabati sa direksyon.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Each makahiya leaf is actually made of many tiny leaflets lined up neatly, just like a feather!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe the outer parts of plants, such as leaves, roots, and stems and identify their role to get water and nutrients from the soil
assignedReviews.reason: The card only describes the feather-like compound shape of makahiya leaves. It does not address the role of leaves (or roots/stems) in getting water and nutrients from the soil, which is the core action of G3-L-5. The shared topic 'leaves' is not enough for direct support.

copy.en:
What do makahiya leaves look like?

Each makahiya leaf is actually made of many tiny leaflets lined up neatly, just like a feather!
copy.tl:
Ano ang hugis ng dahon ng makahiya?

Ang bawat dahon ng makahiya ay gawa sa maraming maliliit na dahon na magkakahanay, parang balahibo!
copy.bis:
Unsay dagway sa dahon sa makahiya?

Ang matag dahon sa makahiya gilangkuban sa daghang gagmayng dahon nga nahan-ay, morag balhibo!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: How does water leave the makahiya leaf's cells?
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the characteristics of living things: they grow, respond, and reproduce
assignedReviews.reason: The card explains a cellular water-loss mechanism behind the leaf folding, but it does not describe the general characteristic of living things responding to stimuli, nor does it mention growth or reproduction. It only touches on a response without framing it as a characteristic of living things.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Tiny salts inside the cell move outward, and water follows them out.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the purpose of specialized structures in plants, such as rhizomes, tubers, thorns, bulbs, and aerial roots
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses a physiological response in a plant leaf, not the purpose of specialized structures such as rhizomes, tubers, thorns, bulbs, or aerial roots. There is no connection to the listed specialized plant structures.

copy.en:
How does water leave the makahiya leaf's cells?

Tiny salts inside the cell move outward, and water follows them out. The cell loses water, goes soft, and the leaf folds!
copy.tl:
Paano nawawala ang tubig sa selula ng makahiya?

May maliliit na asin sa loob ng selula na inililipat sa labas, at sumusunod dito ang tubig. Kaya nawawalan ng tubig ang selula, lumalambot, at tumitiklop ang dahon!
copy.bis:
Unsaon paggawas sa tubig sa selula sa makahiya?

Adunay gagmay nga asin sulod sa selula nga ibalhin sa gawas, ug musunod ang tubig niini. Busa mawad-an og tubig ang selula, muhumok, ug mutiklop ang dahon!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The Malampaya gas field is hiding deep underwater, way out in the sea northwest of Palawan!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: gather information from secondary sources to evaluate how renewable and non-renewable generation of electricity in the Philippines impacts human activities and the environment
assignedReviews.reason: The card only states the location of the Malampaya gas field. It does not provide information about how non-renewable generation of electricity impacts human activities or the environment, nor does it support evaluating such impacts.

copy.en: Did you know? The Malampaya gas field is hiding deep underwater, way out in the sea northwest of Palawan!
copy.tl: Alam mo ba? Ang Malampaya gas field ay nakatago sa ilalim ng dagat, malayo sa hilaga-kanluran ng Palawan!
copy.bis: Nahibaw-an ba nimo? Ang Malampaya gas field nagtago sa ubos sa dagat, layo sa amihanan-kasadpan sa Palawan!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: the father keeps the eggs inside his mouth to keep them safe until they hatch
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify which groups of animals reproduce by giving birth to live young, such as mammals, and which reproduce by laying eggs, such as birds and reptiles
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes a fish that protects eggs, implying egg-laying, but does not identify or compare groups that give birth vs. lay eggs. It does not directly support the classification skill.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: the father keeps the eggs inside his mouth to keep them safe until they hatch
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the characteristics of living things: they grow, respond, and reproduce
assignedReviews.reason: The card shows an example of reproduction (eggs hatching) but does not describe the general characteristics of living things (grow, respond, reproduce). It is a specific behavior, not a description of the characteristic itself.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: the father keeps the eggs inside his mouth to keep them safe until they hatch
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use information from secondary sources to describe examples of how some animals have changed to better suit their environment, such as mimicry or camouflage
assignedReviews.reason: Mouthbrooding is a parental care behavior, not an example of adaptation like mimicry or camouflage. The card does not describe how animals have changed to better suit their environment.

copy.en: In some fish, the father keeps the eggs inside his mouth to keep them safe until they hatch.
copy.tl: May ilang isda na ang lalaki ang nagtatago ng mga itlog sa loob ng kanyang bibig para maprotektahan ang mga ito.
copy.bis: Adunay ubang isda nga ang laki maoy magtago sa mga itlog sa sulod sa iyang baba aron mapanalipdan kini.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Malnutrition happens when the body lacks the right nutrients — eating protein, vegetables, and fruit helps you grow up healthy.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify the basic needs of all living things, such as air, food, water, and shelter
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses nutrition and healthy eating, which touches on food as a need, but it does not identify the basic needs of all living things (air, food, water, shelter) as required by the competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Malnutrition happens when the body lacks the right nutrients — eating protein, vegetables, and fruit helps you grow up healthy.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe in simple terms how the following human body systems work: muscular, skeletal, digestive, circulatory, and respiratory
assignedReviews.reason: The card is about nutrition and malnutrition, not about how the muscular, skeletal, digestive, circulatory, or respiratory systems work. It does not support the competency.

copy.en: Malnutrition happens when the body lacks the right nutrients — eating protein, vegetables, and fruit helps you grow up healthy.
copy.tl: Nangyayari ang malnutrisyon kapag kulang sa tamang sustansya ang katawan — makakatulong ang pagkain ng protina, gulay, at prutas para lumaking malusog.
copy.bis: Mahitabo ang malnutrisyon kung kulang sa husto nga sustansya ang lawas — makatabang ang pagkaon og protina, utanon, ug prutas aron motubo nga himsog.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Malunggay is a plant whose small leaves
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe the outer parts of plants, such as leaves, roots, and stems and identify their role to get water and nutrients from the soil
assignedReviews.reason: The card only mentions that malunggay is a plant with small leaves used in soups. It does not describe observing outer plant parts or their role in absorbing water and nutrients from the soil, which is the focus of G3-L-5.

copy.en: Malunggay is a plant whose small leaves are often added to Filipino soups like tinola.
copy.tl: Ang malunggay ay halamang ang maliliit na dahon ay madalas isama sa mga sabaw tulad ng tinola.
copy.bis: Ang malunggay usa ka tanom nga ang gagmayng dahon kanunay ibutang sa mga sabaw sama sa tinola.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Malunggay leaves are small, rounded, and grow many together along a single stalk.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe the outer parts of plants, such as leaves, roots, and stems and identify their role to get water and nutrients from the soil
assignedReviews.reason: The card only describes the visual appearance of malunggay leaves. It does not address the role of leaves, roots, or stems in obtaining water and nutrients from the soil, which is the core of G3-L-5.

copy.en: Malunggay leaves are small, rounded, and grow many together along a single stalk.
copy.tl: Ang mga dahon ng malunggay ay maliliit, bilugan, at nakatutok nang marami sa isang tangkay.
copy.bis: Ang mga dahon sa malunggay gagmay, lingin, ug daghan nga nagtipun-og sa usa ka tangkay.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A malunggay pod looks a bit like a string bean
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe the outer parts of plants, such as leaves, roots, and stems and identify their role to get water and nutrients from the soil
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions a plant part (pod) and seeds, but does not address leaves, roots, or stems, nor their role in getting water and nutrients from the soil.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: both are long with seeds inside, but they're different plants
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use a table to show how living things can be classified into groups based on similar characteristics (plants including flowering and non-flowering; animals including mammals, reptiles, insects, birds, fish, amphibians; microorganisms including fungi and bacteria)
assignedReviews.reason: The card compares two plants by similar characteristics but does not use a table or classify living things into the named groups required by the competency.

copy.en: A malunggay pod looks a bit like a string bean, both are long with seeds inside, but they're different plants, and malunggay's skin is tougher.
copy.tl: Parang sitaw ang malunggay pod, pareho silang mahaba at may buto sa loob, pero magkaibang halaman ang mga ito, at mas matigas ang balat ng malunggay.
copy.bis: Ang malunggay pod morag batong, parehong taas ug adunay liso sa sulod, apan lahi silang tanom, ug mas gahi ang panit sa malunggay.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: What looks like one malunggay leaf is actually many tiny round leaflets lined up on a stem
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe the outer parts of plants, such as leaves, roots, and stems and identify their role to get water and nutrients from the soil
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes the compound structure of a malunggay leaf (many leaflets on a stem) but does not address the role of leaves, roots, or stems in obtaining water and nutrients from the soil. It shares the topic of plant outer parts but provides no direct instructional support for the competency's function-based objective.

copy.en:
Is a malunggay 'leaf' really just one leaf?

Not quite! What looks like one malunggay leaf is actually many tiny round leaflets lined up on a stem — that's why it looks soft like a fern.
copy.tl:
Isa ba talaga ang dahon ng malunggay?

Hindi pala! Ang tila isang dahon ng malunggay ay binubuo ng maraming maliliit na bilog na dahon na nakahanay sa isang tangkay — kaya mukha itong parang malambot na pako.
copy.bis:
Usa ba jud ang dahon sa kamunggay?

Dili diay! Ang morag usa ka dahon sa kamunggay gilangkoban og daghang gagmay nga lingin nga dahon nga naglinya sa usa ka tangkay — mao nga morag humok nga pako kini.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The sweet carabao mango is made into dried mango
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain the factors affecting the rates of chemical reactions as applied in food preservation and materials production, control of fire, pollution, and corrosion
assignedReviews.reason: The card is about a food product (dried mango) and its export, not about factors affecting rates of chemical reactions, food preservation, materials production, fire control, pollution, or corrosion. copy.en: The sweet carabao mango is made into dried mango, a popular treat exported to other countries.
copy.tl: Ang matamis na carabao mango ay ginagawang dried mango, isang sikat na pasalubong na ipinapadala sa ibang bansa.
copy.bis: Ang tam-is nga carabao mango ginahimong dried mango, usa ka bantog nga pasalubong nga ginapadala sa ubang nasod.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: it can become dried mango, juice, and sweet treats too!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe how changes in solid materials make them useful, such as when they are shaped, pressed, hammered, joined, or cut
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions that mango can be transformed into dried mango, juice, and sweet treats, which are changes in material, but it does not describe how changes in solid materials make them useful (e.g., shaped, pressed, hammered, joined, cut). The examples are about food products, not the specific solid-material changes the competency targets.

copy.en: Mango isn't just for eating fresh — it can become dried mango, juice, and sweet treats too!
copy.tl: Hindi lang sariwa ang paraan ng pagkain ng mangga — pwede rin itong gawing tuyong mangga, juice, at matamis!
copy.bis: Dili lang presko ang pagkaon sa mangga — mahimo usab kining gibulad nga mangga, duga, ug tam-is!

assignedReviews.reason: Bloom season is not a comparison of mammal, bird, and plant life cycles.

assignedReviews.reason: When mangoes bloom is flowering frequency, not pollination, seed production, or plant propagation as methods.

copy.en: Mango trees usually bloom during the hot, dry season.
copy.tl: Karaniwang namumulaklak ang puno ng mangga kapag tag-init o tuyong panahon.
copy.bis: Kasagaran mamulak ang kahoy sa mangga panahon sa init ug ting-init.

assignedReviews.reason: The card only describes the appearance of mango leaves; it does not identify the role of leaves, roots, or stems in getting water and nutrients from the soil, which is the core of the competency.

copy.en: The mango tree has long, shiny green leaves all year round.
copy.tl: Ang punong mangga ay may mahahaba at makikintab na berdeng dahon sa buong taon.
copy.bis: Ang punong mangga adunay tag-as ug masilaw nga lunhaw nga dahon sa tibuok tuig.

assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe the outer parts of plants, such as leaves, roots, and stems and identify their role to get water and nutrients from the soil
assignedReviews.reason: Leafy is named, but not leaves, roots, or stems taking water and nutrients from soil.

copy.en: The mango tree is a big, leafy tree that bursts into flowers before growing sweet mangoes — one of the most loved fruits in the Philippines.
copy.tl: Ang punong mangga ay malaki at mayabong na puno na namumulaklak bago mamunga ng matamis na mangga — isa sa mga paboritong prutas sa Pilipinas.
copy.bis: Ang kahoy nga mangga usa ka dako ug labong nga kahoy nga mamulak una mamunga og tam-is nga mangga — usa sa labing pinangga nga prutas sa Pilipinas.

copy.en: The mangosteen has a thick purple rind that hides soft white flesh inside — like a treasure box for a sweet treat!
copy.tl: Ang mangosteen ay may makapal at lilang balat na nagtatago ng maputi at malambot na laman sa loob!
copy.bis: Ang mangosteen adunay baga ug lila nga panit nga nagtago sa puti ug humok nga unod sa sulod!

assignedReviews.reason: Ray size is not the difference between animals with a backbone and animals without backbones.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The manta ray is the largest ray of all

assignedReviews.reason: The card does not use a drawing or diagram to classify Philippine animals as terrestrial, aquatic, or aerial.

copy.en:
What is the biggest kind of ray?

The manta ray is the largest ray of all — it can stretch up to seven meters wide from wingtip to wingtip!
copy.tl:
Ano ang pinakamalaking uri ng pagi?

Ang manta ray ang pinakamalaking uri ng pagi — umaabot ito ng pitong metro ang lapad mula sa isang pakpak hanggang sa kabila!
copy.bis:
Unsa ang pinakadako nga matang sa pagi?

Ang manta ray mao ang pinakadako nga matang sa pagi — makaabot kini og pito ka metro ang gilapdon gikan sa usa ka pako ngadto sa pikas!

How does ordinary limestone deep underground turn into beautiful marble?

Intense heat and pressure change the limestone deep underground, transforming it into a brand new metamorphic rock called marble!

Paano nagiging magandang marmol ang ordinaryong limestone na nasa ilalim ng lupa?

Binabago ito ng matinding init at presyon sa loob ng lupa, kaya naging metamorphic na bato na tinatawag na marmol!

Unsaon pagkahimo sa ordinaryong limestone nga naa sa ilawom sa yuta nga mahimong nindot nga marmol?

Giusab kini sa kusog nga init ug presyon sa ilawom sa yuta, busa nahimo kini nga metamorphic nga bato nga marmol!
